title: In a Culture Obsessed with Staying Young, We Ignore the Many Benefits of Aging - Nautilus
gist: Teaser excerpt framing the anti-aging industry (worth hundreds of billions of dollars) and Bryan Johnson's biohacking regimen as emblematic of a youth-obsessed culture; the article's promised case for the benefits of aging is not present in the captured text.

insights.claim: The anti-aging industry is worth hundreds of billions of dollars, selling products ranging from 'miracle' supplements to gene therapies.
insights.speaker: Olivia Maurice
insights.so_what: Signals a large consumer longevity market spanning low-evidence supplements to high-end gene therapy.
insights.quote: The anti-aging industry is worth hundreds of billions of dollars, promising everything from “miracle” supplements to gene therapies.

insights.claim: Entrepreneur Bryan Johnson's documented biohacking regimen—cosmetic enhancements, stem cell therapies, total plasma replacement and cloning his own cells—has drawn global fascination and is the most visible face of the immortality pursuit.
insights.speaker: Olivia Maurice
insights.so_what: Celebrity biohackers act as demand-side marketing for experimental longevity therapies.
insights.quote: Johnson has meticulously documented countless treatments in his biohacking regimen, including cosmetic enhancements, stem cell therapies, a total plasma replacement and, most recently, even cloning his own cells.
insights.locator: Johnson has meticulously documented countless treatments

insights.claim: The piece frames a culture-wide obsession with staying young that overlooks the benefits that come with aging.
insights.speaker: Olivia Maurice
insights.so_what: A cultural backlash against youth-maximalism could temper long-run demand narratives for anti-aging products.
insights.quote: Every morning, millions of people wake up hoping to look, think and feel younger than they did yesterday.
